retro:
# PR 12865 retrospective

## What worked
Fresh independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope and the same author-event update. The original public review supplied stable finding IDs and original revision without historical private deliberations. Both finals existed before synthesis. Original/head controls distinguish a valid earlier claim from a correction that resolves it. Source-only Sol review avoided redundant fixtures.

## Deviations and remediation
- Opus cut a duplicated packet line. Full original line was reread, preserving the earlier record. Complete-line reads remain mandatory even for duplicated content.
- GNU sed -i used generated temporary paths under the private fixture parent, not individual pre-write guards. Preserve the fixture revisions; future changes must use explicit preasserted outputs and guarded rename, or precise editing tools.
- Node stdout/stderr were captured in memory and saved after each child completed. This is not persistence from launch. All completed streams/status survived; runtime driver gated exits before decoding. Future dispatches must explicitly require file descriptors opened at asserted unique paths before spawning, including nested helpers.
- Runtime incidental interpreter writes were contained by namespaces but not individually proven guarded. Do not claim absence from an output inventory or equate containment to per-target guards. Python bytecode was disabled; intended node code reads only. Public evidence is narrowed to completed, retained, source-corroborated F1/F2 and Fireworks observations, not blanket suite/guard claims.
- Coordinator inspected F1/F2 payloads before separately opening their child exit receipts, although the fixture itself gated them and the reviewer reported successful exits. Before accepting synthesis the receipts were inspected and all were zero. Future audit order should inspect raw status first as well.
- An unsolicited Claude auto-mode learning dialog appeared after the technical final and intercepted two audit dispatch attempts. Cancelled with Esc, without granting history/repository scans. Native input presence was checked, and the missing audit task was resent once with an activity-aware wait. This is a lifecycle friction report, not a proven Herdr bug.

## Preserved failures and limitations
The first review.py check reported missing node; no r1 execution occurred. r2 explicitly bundled node and obtained its version only in isolation. Failed preflight, raw outputs, fixture revisions and native sessions are retained. Native history and process-only startup memory were not erased or edited. No quota signal occurred.

## Cleanup and improvements
No desktop slots, services or background children were started. Completed subprocess.run children were reaped; the isolated runner exited and its private namespaces ended, verified by owned receipts. No global process or mount discovery. Preserve source/evidence and agent panes. The corrective assignment instructions are retained in PROCESS-CORRECTIONS.md for the outer coordinator's workflow update; do not start another PR from this session.
